# Requirements Quality Checklist: P-RF05 — Personal summary export

**Purpose**: Broad requirements-quality review of spec.md ahead of `/speckit-tasks`/`/speckit-implement` — completeness, clarity, consistency, measurability, scenario/edge-case coverage, non-functional coverage, and assumption validity. Grounded against `docs/input/backend/export-screen-states.md`, `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md`, and this unit's own `plan.md`/`data-model.md` where they reveal gaps in spec.md itself.
**Created**: 2026-10-24
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Is the client's behavior specified when `GET /export/{jobId}/status` itself fails (timeout/offline) mid-poll, as opposed to only covering what happens once the job reaches a terminal state? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK002 Is a bound defined on how long or how many times the sheet keeps polling a status endpoint that keeps failing, before it must settle into a visible state rather than polling indefinitely? [Gap, Spec §SC-005]
- [ ] CHK003 Is the sheet's behavior specified when "Fechar" is tapped while a PDF or raw-data download is already in flight (as opposed to while the job itself is still "Pendente"/"Processando")? [Gap, Spec §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK004 Is a requirement defined for what the sheet shows if the file-share step succeeds in fetching the file but the OS share sheet is dismissed without the user saving/sending it anywhere? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK005 Are requirements defined for an export whose period is large enough to trigger a payload-size failure (`PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`), or is this outcome left entirely unaddressed by spec.md? [Gap, Non-Functional]
- [ ] CHK006 Are requirements defined for initiating, polling, or downloading an export while the device itself is offline, distinct from the mid-session-expiry handling FR-012 already covers? [Gap, Non-Functional]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK007 Is "frequent enough that the user does not perceive the sheet as stuck" (Assumptions §"Status polling") quantified with any concrete bound, or left fully open to interpretation? [Clarity, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK008 Is "the system's normal response time" in SC-005 defined anywhere in spec.md, or does it depend on an external, unstated baseline? [Clarity, Measurability, Spec §SC-005]
- [ ] CHK009 Is "visually and functionally distinct" (FR-007's requirement that the full-failure state differ from FR-006's narrative-only state) defined with concrete, checkable attributes rather than left to subjective judgment? [Clarity, Measurability, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK010 Is "retryable state" (Edge Cases — a failed PDF/raw download) defined precisely enough to distinguish it from the sheet's two non-retryable terminal failure states ("Erro"/FR-007's state), which offer no retry control at all? [Clarity, Spec §Edge Cases]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK011 Does FR-010's enumerated list of states requiring a functional "Fechar" link ("Pendente", "Processando", "Concluído", "Erro", "Período vazio" — five) include FR-007's separately-asserted sixth generic-failure state, or does FR-010's own five-item enumeration conflict with FR-007's claim that "Fechar" is available there too? [Conflict, Spec §FR-007 vs §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK012 Does SC-004's "from any of its five states" match the six-state model the resolved Clarification and FR-007 establish, or does SC-004's count conflict with FR-007's own state? [Conflict, Spec §SC-004 vs §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK013 Do FR-004 ("Pendente" → "Processando") and the Assumptions' statement that the backend's intermediate "data ready, narrative still generating" status is "still part of Processando" agree on exactly one required visual treatment for every status that maps to "Processando"? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004 vs §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK014 Is the Assumption that the status-poll interval "is an implementation detail, not a product requirement" reconcilable with SC-005's requirement that every attempt reach a terminal state "within the system's normal response time" — can SC-005 be verified at all if the polling cadence is unconstrained? [Conflict, Spec §Assumptions vs §SC-005]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK015 Can SC-001's "zero crashes and zero empty or malformed files, across all tested periods" be objectively verified without spec.md defining what range/sample of periods constitutes "all tested periods"? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK016 Is SC-002's "clear explanation of what happened" measurable against any criterion, or does it restate FR-006's requirement without adding a testable threshold? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK017 Does SC-003 add a measurable criterion beyond FR-003's own wording, or is it a non-additive restatement that could be collapsed without losing test coverage? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK018 Are requirements defined for a job that fails immediately after creation — i.e., transitions straight to the FR-007 failure state without the sheet ever visibly passing through "Processando"? [Coverage, Gap]
- [ ] CHK019 Is it specified, as a requirement rather than only an Assumption aside, that reopening the export sheet for the same period after a prior export's sheet was closed always creates a fresh job rather than attaching to any job left running server-side? [Coverage, Spec §Assumptions "Resuming an export after leaving the sheet"]
- [ ] CHK020 Is a requirement defined for what the user sees in the interval between tapping the download icon and the "Pendente" state rendering, or is a gap-free transition assumed without being stated? [Coverage, Clarity, Spec §FR-004]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK021 Is the session-expiry requirement (FR-012) specific enough to state what happens if the session expires while a PDF/raw download is itself in flight, as distinct from expiry during polling? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK022 Is the retry affordance for a failed download (Edge Cases) specified as re-tapping the same "Baixar..." button versus a distinct new control, or is this left unstated? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK023 Is it specified whether an in-flight export's period stays fixed to what it was at request time if the user could otherwise change My Records' active date filter while the sheet remains open? [Edge Case, Gap]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK024 Are any accessibility requirements (e.g., screen-reader labeling, focus handling) specified for the sheet's six states, or is this dimension entirely unaddressed? [Gap, Non-Functional]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK025 Is RF07's existing session-expiration handling validated in spec.md as sufficient for the two sheet states (FR-007's full-failure state, "Período vazio") that did not exist in RF07's own original scope? [Assumption, Spec §FR-012]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [ ] CHK026 Does the Edge Cases bullet on repeated download-icon taps resolve which single behavior is required — "treated as a no-op" or "reopens the same in-flight sheet" — or does presenting both as options leave the actual requirement ambiguous? [Ambiguity, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK027 Is User Story 3's claim that "no job ever appears to run" for an empty period reconciled with FR-003/the backend contract's own `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD` failure being returned from the job-creation call itself — does spec.md clarify whether a job object can momentarily exist server-side despite this wording, or is this an unresolved ambiguity? [Ambiguity, Spec §US3 vs §FR-003]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference

370	## Dependencies & Execution Order
371	
372	### Phase Dependencies
373	
374	- **Setup (Phase 1)**: No dependencies.
375	- **Foundational (Phase 2)**: Depends on Setup. BLOCKS every user story phase — unlike most features, this
376	  phase contains the entire feature's implementation (T002–T026), because `ExportState`'s sealed-class switch
377	  in `export_sheet.dart` must be exhaustive from first compile.
378	- **User Stories (Phases 3–5)**: All depend on Foundational completion. Each phase's tests are independent of
379	  the others' and can be written/run in any order or in parallel by different people.
380	- **Polish (Phase 6)**: Depends on all three user story phases.
381	
382	### Within Phase 2 (Foundational)
383	
384	T002 → T003 · T004/T005/T006 independent of T002 · T006 → T007 · (T002,T004,T006) → T008 → T009 ·
385	(T004,T008) → T010 → T011 · T005 → T012 → T013 · T014/T015 independent · (T004,T005,T010,T012,T014,T015) →
386	T016 · (T006,T008,T010,T012,T016) → T017 · T018–T023 independent of each other · (T014,T015,T016,T017,
387	T018–T023) → T024 → T025 → T026.
388	
389	### Within Each User Story Phase
390	
391	Bloc test tasks within a phase (T027–T030, T033–T038, T042, T049–T050) share one file
392	(`export_bloc_test.dart`) and are added sequentially, not in parallel, to avoid conflicting edits. Widget test
393	tasks (T031, T039, T040, T043) are each their own file and have no dependency on the bloc test tasks.
394	
395	### Parallel Opportunities
396	
397	- All of T018–T023 (the six state-view widgets) can be built in parallel — six independent files, no
398	  cross-dependency.
399	- T002/T004/T005/T006/T014/T015 (entity, two domain interfaces, `ApiClient` extension, event/state classes)
400	  have no dependency on each other and can start together once Setup is done.
401	- Within each user story phase, the widget test task(s) can run in parallel with that phase's bloc test
402	  tasks, since they touch different files.
403	- The three manual-verification tasks (T032, T041, T044) can be performed by different people once Phase 2's
404	  checkpoint is reached.
405	
406	---
407	
408	## Parallel Example: Phase 2 widget layer
409	
410	```bash
411	Task: "Create export_pending_view.dart"
412	Task: "Create export_processing_view.dart"
413	Task: "Create export_concluded_view.dart"
414	Task: "Create export_narrative_failed_view.dart"
415	Task: "Create export_failed_view.dart"
416	Task: "Create export_empty_period_view.dart"
417	# All six (T018–T023) are independent files — only export_sheet.dart (T024) needs all six done first.
418	```
419	
420	---
421	
422	## Implementation Strategy
423	
424	### MVP scope
425	
426	Because spec.md assigns **P1 to both User Story 1 and User Story 2** (US2 is called out explicitly as its own
427	acceptance criterion, not a nice-to-have), the smallest responsible MVP is **Phase 1 + Phase 2 + Phase 3 (US1)
428	+ Phase 4 (US2)** — a narrative-failure falling back to raw data is as core to RF05's trust story as the PDF
429	path itself. User Story 3 (empty-period handling, P2) is the first increment after that.
430	
431	### Incremental delivery
432	
433	1. Setup + Foundational (Phases 1–2) → the full feature compiles, is wired into "Meus Registros", passes its
434	   own tests.
435	2. Add US1's tests + manual pass (Phase 3) → confident in the narrative-PDF happy path. **MVP checkpoint 1.**
436	3. Add US2's tests + manual pass (Phase 4) → confident the AI narrative can never block the user's own data.
437	   **Full MVP.**
438	4. Add US3's tests + manual pass (Phase 5) → confident the empty-period edge case never shows a spinner.
439	5. Polish (Phase 6) → `flutter analyze`, architecture tests, RNF07 coverage gate, remaining edge cases.
440	
441	### Parallel team strategy
442	
443	With multiple people: one completes Setup + Foundational alone (it's one tightly-coupled unit, hard to split
444	usefully). Once Phase 2's checkpoint is reached, up to three people can each own one user story phase's
445	tests + manual verification in parallel — none of Phases 3–5 touch each other's test files except the shared
446	`export_bloc_test.dart` (coordinate on that one file, or have one person own all bloc-test additions).

# Tasks: P-RF05 — Personal summary export

**Input**: Design documents from `/specs/010-personal-summary-export/`
**Prerequisites**: plan.md, spec.md, research.md, data-model.md, contracts/, quickstart.md (all present)

**Tests**: Included. RNF07 (≥80% domain coverage) and RNF09 (Either + full error-scenario coverage) are
gates this plan explicitly carries into tasks, and every contract in `contracts/` enumerates its own numbered
test-scenario table — these are treated as required deliverables, not optional extras.

**Organization**: `ExportState` is a single Dart `sealed class` with six variants, and the one widget that
renders it (`export_sheet.dart`) must switch over all six exhaustively from the moment it compiles — so the
full domain/data/bloc/widget implementation is **one indivisible unit** (Phase 2, Foundational) rather than
something that can be built one user story at a time. Each user story phase (3–5) instead adds the
**automated tests and manual verification that specifically prove that story's acceptance scenarios**,
independently of the other stories' tests — this is this feature's actual "independently testable" seam,
given its architecture.

## Format: `[ID] [P?] [Story] Description`

- **[P]**: Can run in parallel (different files, no dependency on an incomplete task)
- **[Story]**: US1 / US2 / US3, per spec.md's priorities (US1 and US2 are both P1; US3 is P2)

## Path Conventions

Single Flutter app. `lib/features/export/` (new, 3-layer), `lib/core/network/api_client.dart` (extended),
`lib/core/di/service_locator.dart` (extended), `lib/features/records/presentation/pages/records_page.dart`
(extended). Tests mirror `lib/` under `test/`, matching this repo's existing `entries/`/`chat`/`records`
layout.

---

## Phase 1: Setup

- [ ] T001 Add `share_plus: ^13.3.1` to `pubspec.yaml`'s dependencies (research.md R2) and run
  `fvm flutter pub get` — `path_provider: ^2.1.5` is already present, no other dependency change.

---

## Phase 2: Foundational (Blocking Prerequisites)

**Purpose**: The complete `export/` feature (domain → data → bloc → widgets) plus the two cross-cutting
extensions (`ApiClient.downloadFile()`, `records_page.dart`'s icon wiring) that every user story depends on.
No user story's acceptance scenario is observable, through the UI or a bloc test, until this phase is done.

### Domain layer

- [ ] T002 [P] Create `ExportJobStatus` (`pending`/`processing`/`dataReady`/`done`/`error`), `NarrativeStatus`
  (`pending`/`processing`/`done`/`failed`/`skipped`) and `ExportSheetState`
  (`pendente`/`processando`/`concluido`/`erroNarrativa`/`erroCompleto`/`periodoVazio`) enums; the `ExportJob`
  `Equatable` entity (`jobId` `String`, `status` `ExportJobStatus`, `narrativeStatus` `NarrativeStatus`,
  `entryCount` `int?`, `errorCode` `String?`, `narrativeErrorCode` `String?`, `downloadAvailable` `bool`); and
  the pure `ExportJobSheetState.sheetState` extension implementing `export-screen-states.md`'s table verbatim
  (`pending`→`pendente`; `processing`→`processando`; `dataReady`→`processando` regardless of
  `narrativeStatus`; `done`+`done`→`concluido`; `done`+(`failed`|`skipped`)→`erroNarrativa`; `error`→
  `erroCompleto`) in `lib/features/export/domain/entities/export_job.dart` (data-model.md, research.md R4).
- [ ] T003 [P] Write unit tests covering `ExportJob.sheetState`'s full 6-row mapping as a total, pure
  function (zero constructor dependencies, zero I/O) in
  `test/features/export/domain/entities/export_job_test.dart` (research.md R4, RNF07).
- [ ] T004 [P] Create the `ExportFormat` enum (`pdf`, `raw`) and the `ExportRepository` abstract interface —
  `Future<Either<Failure, String>> create({required DateTime? periodStart, required DateTime? periodEnd})`,
  `Future<Either<Failure, ExportJob>> status(String jobId)`,
  `Future<Either<Failure, Uint8List>> download({required String jobId, required ExportFormat format})` — in
  `lib/features/export/domain/repositories/export_repository.dart` (contracts/export-repository.md).
- [ ] T005 [P] Create the `ExportFileRepository` abstract interface —
  `Future<Either<Failure, Unit>> share({required Uint8List bytes, required ExportFormat format})` — in
  `lib/features/export/domain/repositories/export_file_repository.dart` (contracts/export-repository.md).

### Core network

- [ ] T006 [P] Add `Future<Either<Failure, Uint8List>> downloadFile(String function, {List<String>?
  pathSegments, Map<String, dynamic>? queryParameters, AuthMode authMode = AuthMode.userSession})` to
  `lib/core/network/api_client.dart` (`call()`/`sseStream()` unchanged): leg 1 is a `GET` to `function` with
  `followRedirects: false` and `validateStatus: (status) => status != null && status < 400`, sending the same
  `apikey`/`Authorization` headers `call()` already sends; a non-`302` status or a missing `location` header
  returns `Left(ValidationFailure(message: 'Malformed response: expected a 302 redirect', requestId: ''))`;

## Dependencies & Execution Order

### Phase Dependencies

- **Setup (Phase 1)**: No dependencies.
- **Foundational (Phase 2)**: Depends on Setup. BLOCKS every user story phase — unlike most features, this
  phase contains the entire feature's implementation (T002–T026), because `ExportState`'s sealed-class switch
  in `export_sheet.dart` must be exhaustive from first compile.
- **User Stories (Phases 3–5)**: All depend on Foundational completion. Each phase's tests are independent of
  the others' and can be written/run in any order or in parallel by different people.
- **Polish (Phase 6)**: Depends on all three user story phases.

### Within Phase 2 (Foundational)

T002 → T003 · T004/T005/T006 independent of T002 · T006 → T007 · (T002,T004,T006) → T008 → T009 ·
(T004,T008) → T010 → T011 · T005 → T012 → T013 · T014/T015 independent · (T004,T005,T010,T012,T014,T015) →
T016 · (T006,T008,T010,T012,T016) → T017 · T018–T023 independent of each other · (T014,T015,T016,T017,
T018–T023) → T024 → T025 → T026.

### Within Each User Story Phase

Bloc test tasks within a phase (T027–T030, T033–T038, T042, T049–T050) share one file
(`export_bloc_test.dart`) and are added sequentially, not in parallel, to avoid conflicting edits. Widget test
tasks (T031, T039, T040, T043) are each their own file and have no dependency on the bloc test tasks.

### Parallel Opportunities

- All of T018–T023 (the six state-view widgets) can be built in parallel — six independent files, no
  cross-dependency.
- T002/T004/T005/T006/T014/T015 (entity, two domain interfaces, `ApiClient` extension, event/state classes)
  have no dependency on each other and can start together once Setup is done.
- Within each user story phase, the widget test task(s) can run in parallel with that phase's bloc test
  tasks, since they touch different files.
- The three manual-verification tasks (T032, T041, T044) can be performed by different people once Phase 2's
  checkpoint is reached.

---

## Parallel Example: Phase 2 widget layer

```bash
Task: "Create export_pending_view.dart"
Task: "Create export_processing_view.dart"
Task: "Create export_concluded_view.dart"
Task: "Create export_narrative_failed_view.dart"
Task: "Create export_failed_view.dart"
Task: "Create export_empty_period_view.dart"
# All six (T018–T023) are independent files — only export_sheet.dart (T024) needs all six done first.
```

---

## Implementation Strategy

### MVP scope

Because spec.md assigns **P1 to both User Story 1 and User Story 2** (US2 is called out explicitly as its own
acceptance criterion, not a nice-to-have), the smallest responsible MVP is **Phase 1 + Phase 2 + Phase 3 (US1)
+ Phase 4 (US2)** — a narrative-failure falling back to raw data is as core to RF05's trust story as the PDF
path itself. User Story 3 (empty-period handling, P2) is the first increment after that.

### Incremental delivery

1. Setup + Foundational (Phases 1–2) → the full feature compiles, is wired into "Meus Registros", passes its
   own tests.
2. Add US1's tests + manual pass (Phase 3) → confident in the narrative-PDF happy path. **MVP checkpoint 1.**
3. Add US2's tests + manual pass (Phase 4) → confident the AI narrative can never block the user's own data.
   **Full MVP.**
4. Add US3's tests + manual pass (Phase 5) → confident the empty-period edge case never shows a spinner.
5. Polish (Phase 6) → `flutter analyze`, architecture tests, RNF07 coverage gate, remaining edge cases.

### Parallel team strategy

With multiple people: one completes Setup + Foundational alone (it's one tightly-coupled unit, hard to split
usefully). Once Phase 2's checkpoint is reached, up to three people can each own one user story phase's
tests + manual verification in parallel — none of Phases 3–5 touch each other's test files except the shared
`export_bloc_test.dart` (coordinate on that one file, or have one person own all bloc-test additions).

| Addition | Why Needed | Simpler Alternative Rejected Because |

1	# Research: P-RF05 — Personal summary export
2	
3	Phase 0 output. Each item is a reasonable technical decision made under Constitution Principle I ("where
4	these documents are silent, implementers MUST make a reasonable technical decision rather than block on
5	clarification"). None reopens spec.md's own already-resolved Clarification (the FR-007 full-failure state) —
6	each item below fills in a mechanical detail that Clarification, the OpenAPI contract, `export-screen-
7	states.md`, or the prototype extract leaves open.
8	
9	## R1 — How the download endpoint's 302-redirect-to-signed-URL is fetched without leaking auth headers
10	
11	**Decision**: `ApiClient` (core/network) gains one new method, `downloadFile(...)`, built the same way
12	`sseStream()` (RF04) added a second transport shape on top of the existing `call()` — a two-step fetch, never
13	a single `Dio.request<Map>()` (which expects JSON and would fail to parse PDF/raw bytes):
14	1. Request `GET /export/{jobId}/download?format=pdf|raw` with `followRedirects: false` and
15	   `validateStatus: (status) => status != null && status < 400` (so a 302 is accepted, not thrown as a
16	   `DioException`), sending the same `apikey`/`Authorization` headers every other call already sends — this
17	   leg talks to *our* backend function, so it goes through the exact same auth story as `call()`.
18	2. Read the `Location` response header. If the status was not 302 or the header is missing, treat it as a
19	   malformed response (`ValidationFailure`) — the backend's own contract only documents a 302 success shape.
20	3. Issue a **second**, header-less `Dio.request<List<int>>()` straight to that signed Storage URL, with
21	   `responseType: ResponseType.bytes` and no `apikey`/`Authorization` headers at all.
22	4. Return `Either<Failure, Uint8List>` — `Right(bytes)` on a 2xx from step 3; any failure from either leg maps
23	   through `_mapException` (step 1: identical to `call()`'s existing JSON-error path, so `AUTH_EXPIRED`/
24	   `NOT_FOUND`/etc. all resolve through the normal `ErrorMapper`) or a new, generic retryable
25	   `NetworkTimeoutFailure` (step 2/3: the storage leg never speaks this app's `{code, message, retryable}`
26	   error envelope, so there is nothing for `ErrorMapper` to parse — Edge Cases only asks that "the
27	   corresponding button returns to a retryable state", not that the exact backend error code survive a
28	   fetch that never reached the backend).
29	
30	**Rationale**: the signed URL already encodes its own short-lived auth via query parameters (that is the
31	entire point of a signed URL); forwarding this app's `apikey`/`SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`/user bearer token to a
32	third-party Storage host it was never intended for is an unnecessary credential-exposure surface Principle
33	III's spirit ("narrowly-accessed contract... prevents... credential leakage") argues against, and `dio`'s
34	default redirect-following would do exactly that by keeping the original request's headers across the
35	redirect. Disabling auto-redirect and manually re-issuing a clean request is the only way to control which
36	headers reach which host. This mirrors `sseStream()`'s own precedent of adding a second, download-agnostic
37	transport primitive to `ApiClient` rather than growing a parallel HTTP stack per feature.
38	
39	**Alternatives considered**: letting `dio` auto-follow the redirect — rejected for the header-leak reason
40	above; a dedicated plain `http`/`http_client` package call for the storage leg — rejected, `dio` already does
41	a header-less byte-stream GET with no new dependency; parsing the Storage response as JSON first — rejected,
42	both `format=pdf` and `format=raw` are binary/text payloads to save to disk, not API responses with a
43	`{data: ...}` envelope.
44	
45	## R2 — Saving/sharing the downloaded bytes (no download/file package exists yet)
46	
47	**Decision**: add `share_plus: ^13.3.1` (new dependency; `path_provider` is already in `pubspec.yaml`, added
48	for the audio pipeline). A new data-layer class, `ExportFileRepositoryImpl` (behind a domain interface,
49	`ExportFileRepository`, so `ExportBloc` depends on it through the same mockable-repository shape every other
50	bloc already uses — never a bare plugin wrapper), writes the downloaded bytes to
51	`(await getTemporaryDirectory()).path` under a derived filename, then calls `Share.shareXFiles([XFile(path)])`
52	— the OS share sheet, satisfying the Assumption "trigger[s] the platform's standard way of saving or sharing a
53	downloaded file." The extension is taken from the response's own `content-type`/`content-disposition` header
54	when present, falling back to `.pdf` for `format=pdf` and `.json` for `format=raw` (every other endpoint in
55	this backend's contract speaks JSON; nothing in the OpenAPI spec names a different shape for the raw export).
56	
57	**Rationale**: Constitution Principle II explicitly leaves "local cache... secure storage" (and, by the same
58	"choices not fixed here" logic, a file-share mechanism — no fixed package is named for this anywhere in
59	`docs/input/`) as an open implementation decision, the same category `image_picker`/`record`/`whisper_ggml`
60	were already added under in earlier units. `share_plus` is the de-facto standard Flutter package for exactly
61	this job (iOS `UIActivityViewController`), needs no new permission beyond what sharing already implies, and
62	composes with the already-present `path_provider` rather than introducing a second temp-file mechanism.
63	
64	**Alternatives considered**: `open_file`/`open_filex` (opens a file in another app directly rather than
65	offering the OS share sheet) — rejected, narrower than "save or share" and typically requires a file-
66	association/viewer app to exist, which this PDF-generating unit cannot assume; writing to a permanent
67	app-documents path and leaving the user to find it in Files.app — rejected, no in-app file browser exists or
68	is in scope (Assumptions: "not responsible for building a custom in-app file viewer"), so a silent write with
69	no share/save prompt would be a dead end for the user.
70	
71	## R3 — Status-polling mechanism and interval
72	
73	**Decision**: `ExportBloc` polls `GET /export/{jobId}/status` through a self-rescheduling chain of internal
74	events, not `Timer.periodic` — the exact shape `RecordsBloc`'s own search debounce already establishes
75	(`Timer(duration, () => add(Event()))`, re-armed from inside the handler, cancelled in `close()`). The instant
76	`ExportRequested` is handled, the bloc emits `ExportPending()` synchronously (FR-004's "immediately after the
77	request"), awaits the `POST /export/summary` call, and on success immediately dispatches one
78	`ExportStatusPollTicked()` (no initial delay — the POST round-trip has already elapsed). Each tick's handler
79	calls `GET status` once; if the resulting job is not yet in a terminal state (`sheetState` below), it arms
80	`Timer(const Duration(seconds: 2), () => add(const ExportStatusPollTicked()))` for the next tick. Sequential,
81	never overlapping — a slow response is fully awaited before the next tick is even scheduled.
82	
83	**Rationale**: spec.md's own Assumptions state this interval is "an implementation detail, not a product
84	requirement, as long as it is frequent enough that the user does not perceive the sheet as stuck" — 2 seconds
85	comfortably satisfies that for an AI-narrative job (seconds-to-tens-of-seconds scale) without hammering the
86	backend. Routing every tick through the bloc's own event pipeline (rather than a bare `Timer` mutating state
87	directly) keeps `ExportBloc` testable with `bloc_test` the same way `RecordsBloc`'s debounce already is —
88	`add()` from a `Timer` callback is this codebase's own established pattern, not a new one.
89	
90	**Alternatives considered**: `Timer.periodic` — rejected, risks overlapping requests if a status call ever
91	takes longer than the interval (the sequential self-reschedule shape cannot overlap by construction); a
92	shorter interval (e.g. 500 ms) — rejected as needless backend load for a job whose fastest realistic path
93	(empty-period) never reaches polling at all (R6) and whose slowest path is bounded by an AI call, not network
94	latency.
95	
96	## R4 — `ExportJob`'s pure sheet-state derivation, and the sixth, Clarification-resolved state
97	
98	**Decision**: a pure domain extension, `ExportJob.sheetState`, mirrors the already-established
99	`DateRangeBounds.boundsAt`/`SyncBadge.derive` pattern (a total function over an enum, zero I/O, directly
100	unit-testable for RNF07) and implements `export-screen-states.md`'s table verbatim:
101	
102	| `status` | `narrativeStatus` | `sheetState` |
103	|---|---|---|
104	| `pending` | (any) | `pendente` |
105	| `processing` | (any) | `processando` |
106	| `dataReady` | `processing` | `processando` (Assumption: no early download link; still visually "Processando") |
107	| `done` | `done` | `concluido` |
108	| `done` | `failed` or `skipped` | `erroNarrativa` (FR-006 — the prototype's single "Erro" state) |
109	| `error` | — | `erroCompleto` (FR-007 — the Clarification-resolved sixth state) |
110	
111	`erroCompleto` is a distinct enum value from `erroNarrativa` even though the prototype's own catalog names
112	only one "Erro" state — this directly encodes spec.md's resolved Clarification ("reusing the error color/icon
113	family, with copy distinct from FR-006's... no PDF/raw buttons, and only... Fechar"). `ExportBloc` additionally
114	reaches `erroCompleto` from two paths `ExportJob.sheetState` never sees at all, because no job/jobId exists
115	yet at that point: an `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD`-shaped `POST` failure instead maps to a seventh, job-independent
116	bloc state, `periodoVazio` (R6), and any *other* `POST /export/summary` failure (timeout, offline, rate-
117	limited, ...) maps directly to the bloc's `erroCompleto` state without ever creating a job (R6).
118	
119	**Rationale**: putting the five-row mapping in the domain layer as a pure getter (not duplicated inline in
120	`ExportBloc` or a widget's `switch`) is the same choice `RecordsBloc` already made for `SyncBadge.derive` and
121	`DateRangeBounds` — directly testable, and the one place this mapping's correctness is asserted. Keeping
122	`erroCompleto`/`periodoVazio` as *bloc*-level states rather than trying to force them into `ExportJob` is
123	necessary because both can occur with no `ExportJob` ever existing (a job is never created for an empty
124	period, and a POST that never got as far as `202 Accepted` never produced a `jobId` to poll).
125	
126	**Alternatives considered**: reusing one single `erro` state for both FR-006 and FR-007 with a boolean flag —
127	rejected, directly contradicts the resolved Clarification's explicit "this state MUST be visually and
128	functionally distinct from FR-006's narrative-only failure" (FR-007); modeling `periodoVazio` as a sentinel
129	`ExportJob` (e.g. a fake job with no id) — rejected, forces every `ExportJob` consumer to special-case a
130	value that was never a real job, when the bloc's own sealed `ExportState` already has a natural home for it.
131	
132	## R5 — Routing every `POST /export/summary` failure other than `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD` to FR-007
133	
134	**Decision**: if the initial `POST /export/summary` call itself fails with `ExportEmptyPeriodFailure`, the
135	bloc emits `ExportEmptyPeriod()` (FR-003) and polls nothing. If it fails with `AuthExpiredFailure` after the
136	repository's one silent-refresh retry already failed, the bloc fires `reauthRequired` (R7) same as every other
137	failure path in this app, *and* also emits `ExportFailed()` — the session overlay takes over visually (FR-012)
138	regardless of what state sits underneath it. For every other failure shape (`NetworkTimeoutFailure`,
139	`NetworkOfflineFailure`, `RateLimitedFailure`, `ValidationFailure`, ...), the bloc emits `ExportFailed()`
140	(FR-007's generic, job-independent failure state) directly — no job/jobId exists, so "no data was produced" is
141	true by construction, matching FR-007's own wording precisely.
142	
143	**Rationale**: spec.md's FRs/Assumptions describe FR-007 only in terms of a job that "fails entirely," which
144	textually presumes a job exists — but the spec is silent on what happens if the export is never even accepted
145	in the first place (e.g. the device goes offline the instant the download icon is tapped). Reasonable
146	technical judgment under Principle I: a request that never produced a job has, definitionally, produced no
147	data and no narrative — the exact condition FR-007 itself describes — so reusing that same terminal state
148	(rather than inventing an eighth, undocumented sheet state) is the simplest construction that satisfies FR-010
149	("Fechar... present... in every one of the five sheet states") without adding a state the prototype's own
150	five-state catalog, plus the one Clarification-resolved addition, doesn't already cover.
151	
152	**Alternatives considered**: a distinct "could not even start" state — rejected, no product input describes
153	one, and FR-007's own generic, errorCode-agnostic copy ("shown the same way regardless of the backend's
154	specific error code") already reads naturally for this case too; silently retrying the POST — rejected, not
155	asked for anywhere, and would hide a real failure (e.g. persistent offline) behind an indefinite "Pendente",
156	directly risking SC-005's "never... indefinitely" guarantee.

158	## R6 — Why `ExportBloc` is sheet-scoped (one new instance per `showModalBottomSheet` call), not a singleton
159	
160	**Decision**: `ExportBloc` is `get_it`-registered with `registerFactory` (a fresh instance per
161	`getIt<ExportBloc>()` call) — the same registration shape `InsertionModalBloc`/`VaultBloc` already use for
162	their own modal/one-shot screens — and is provided directly above the bottom sheet's content
163	(`BlocProvider<ExportBloc>(create: (_) => getIt<ExportBloc>()..add(ExportRequested(...)))`, mirroring
164	`FilterSheet`'s own self-contained-sheet shape). Its polling `Timer` is cancelled in `close()` (same pattern
165	`RecordsBloc` already uses for its debounce timer); `close()` fires the moment the sheet's `BlocProvider` is
166	removed from the tree (i.e. the sheet is dismissed), so no poll ever fires for a sheet the user has already
167	closed — directly satisfying the Edge Case "the app does not keep polling it in background once the sheet is
168	gone... not treated as the 'current' export if the sheet is reopened." FR-011's "repeated taps... MUST NOT
169	create multiple concurrent export jobs" is satisfied one layer up, in `_RecordsPageState`: a simple
170	`bool _isOpeningExportSheet` guard (set before `await showModalBottomSheet(...)`, cleared after) around the
171	download icon's `onPressed`, identical in spirit to the guard every `IconButton`-triggered async action in
172	this codebase already needs against a double-tap racing a single `await`.
173	
174	**Rationale**: the Edge Case's own wording offers two acceptable shapes ("treated as a no-op (or reopens the
175	same in-flight sheet)"); the no-op-via-guarded-tap shape is simpler and needs no new cross-sheet state
176	(reusing a leftover job id across sheet instances would directly contradict the Assumptions' own "Reopening the
177	export sheet afterward is a fresh request; it does not need to return to a leftover job" — the two Edge
178	Cases/Assumptions together only make sense together if "in flight" here means "the sheet currently on screen,"
179	not "any job the backend still happens to be processing"). A page-level singleton bloc (reused across sheet
180	opens, like `EntriesRepositoryImpl`'s `cachedEntries`) was considered and rejected because the ephemeral,
181	one-shot-per-open shape of the export sheet (Key Entities: "ephemeral... never shown anywhere outside the
182	export sheet") has no state worth surviving a dismiss — unlike `EntriesRepositoryImpl`'s cache, which exists
183	specifically to survive across many screen visits.
184	
185	**Alternatives considered**: a `RecordsBloc`-owned export sub-state (folding export into the existing bloc
186	entirely) — rejected, conflates two independently-failing, independently-lifetimed concerns into one state
187	class, the same reasoning RF04's research.md R7 already used to keep `ChatBloc`/`ChatSessionsBloc` apart; a
188	page-level singleton `ExportBloc` surviving sheet dismissal — rejected per the Assumptions conflict above.
189	
190	## R7 — Reusing the exact `reauthRequired`/silent-refresh-retry shape, start to finish
191	
192	**Decision**: `ExportRepositoryImpl` wraps every one of its three calls (`create`/`status`/`download`) in the
193	identical `_retryAfterSilentRefresh` shape `EntriesRepositoryImpl` already established (exactly one retry via
194	`SessionRepository.refresh()` on a first-attempt `AuthExpiredFailure`; a second `AuthExpiredFailure` after that
195	retry is returned as-is, no loop). `ExportBloc` owns its own one-shot `_reauthController`/`reauthRequired`
196	stream (`StreamController<void>.broadcast()`, closed in `close()`), fired with `if (failure is
197	AuthExpiredFailure) _reauthController.add(null);` at every call site that can produce one — the exact line
198	`RecordsBloc` already uses three times over. The sheet widget (`ExportSheet`, a `StatefulWidget`) subscribes
199	to it in `initState()` exactly as `RecordsPage` already does for `RecordsBloc`, dispatching
200	`SessionBloc.add(const AuthExpiredDetected())` — `SessionBloc` is provided above `MaterialApp.router` in
201	`main.dart`, so it is reachable from a bottom sheet's `BuildContext` exactly as it is from any full-screen
202	route, and the resulting "Sessão expirada" overlay (pushed via the root `NavigatorKey`) renders above the
203	sheet automatically, needing no export-specific wiring.
204	
205	**Rationale**: FR-012 asks for exactly this — the existing RF07 mechanism "tak[ing] over exactly as it does
206	elsewhere on the screen" — so the correct implementation is to reuse the identical mechanism verbatim, not to
207	build a parallel one. "Resume reflecting the export job's actual status once re-authenticated" falls out of
208	this construction for free: `ExportRepositoryImpl`'s own retry-after-refresh means a mid-poll `AUTH_EXPIRED`
209	that the silent refresh *can* recover from is invisible to `ExportBloc` entirely (the very next poll tick
210	simply succeeds with fresh credentials); only a refresh that itself fails surfaces the overlay, and once the
211	user re-authenticates through it, the next scheduled poll tick (already armed before the failure, since the
212	`Timer` from the prior successful tick is independent of this one failing) picks the real status back up with
213	no bespoke "resume" code needed.
214	
215	**Alternatives considered**: having `ExportBloc` itself call `SessionRepository.refresh()` — rejected, 
216	duplicates logic `EntriesRepositoryImpl`/`ChatRepositoryImpl` already centralize at the repository layer,
217	and would be the first bloc in this codebase to depend on `SessionRepository` directly, contradicting the
218	established "blocs never touch `SessionRepository`" shape (research.md precedent, `RecordsBloc`'s own
219	docstring).
220	
221	## R8 — How the download icon learns the current period, and why no new `go_router` route is added
222	
223	**Decision**: the export sheet is opened from `RecordsPage`'s existing header `IconButton` (currently an inert
224	placeholder, `records_page.dart`'s `_Header`), not via a new route. `_RecordsPageState` reads
225	`context.read<RecordsBloc>().state`'s `dateRange` (a `DateRangeOption`, already RF06's own filter model) at
226	the moment the icon is tapped, converts it with the already-existing, pure `DateRangeBounds.boundsAt(DateTime.
227	now())` extension (RF06) into `(from: DateTime?, to: DateTime?)`, and passes those two nullable values straight
228	through to `ExportSheet(periodStart: ..., periodEnd: ...)` as `showModalBottomSheet`'s builder argument — the
229	sheet's own `ExportBloc` dispatches `ExportRequested(periodStart, periodEnd)` from its `initState`.
230	
231	**Rationale**: spec.md's own Assumptions state the export "exports whatever period My Records' own active
232	date filter currently represents... rather than offering a separate period picker inside the sheet itself" —
233	`RecordsBloc`'s `dateRange` is already the single source of truth for that filter (FR-002's own wording,
234	RF06), and `DateRangeBounds` already converts it to concrete bounds for every other consumer that needs them.
235	Reusing it here needs zero new domain logic. A bottom sheet (not a route) matches both the prototype
236	("bottom sheet over Tela 4") and this codebase's own precedent for `FilterSheet` — no `go_router` route exists
237	for RF06's filter sheet either, for the same reason.
238

# Research: P-RF05 — Personal summary export

Phase 0 output. Each item is a reasonable technical decision made under Constitution Principle I ("where
these documents are silent, implementers MUST make a reasonable technical decision rather than block on
clarification"). None reopens spec.md's own already-resolved Clarification (the FR-007 full-failure state) —
each item below fills in a mechanical detail that Clarification, the OpenAPI contract, `export-screen-
states.md`, or the prototype extract leaves open.

## R1 — How the download endpoint's 302-redirect-to-signed-URL is fetched without leaking auth headers

**Decision**: `ApiClient` (core/network) gains one new method, `downloadFile(...)`, built the same way
`sseStream()` (RF04) added a second transport shape on top of the existing `call()` — a two-step fetch, never
a single `Dio.request<Map>()` (which expects JSON and would fail to parse PDF/raw bytes):
1. Request `GET /export/{jobId}/download?format=pdf|raw` with `followRedirects: false` and
   `validateStatus: (status) => status != null && status < 400` (so a 302 is accepted, not thrown as a
   `DioException`), sending the same `apikey`/`Authorization` headers every other call already sends — this
   leg talks to *our* backend function, so it goes through the exact same auth story as `call()`.
2. Read the `Location` response header. If the status was not 302 or the header is missing, treat it as a
   malformed response (`ValidationFailure`) — the backend's own contract only documents a 302 success shape.
3. Issue a **second**, header-less `Dio.request<List<int>>()` straight to that signed Storage URL, with
   `responseType: ResponseType.bytes` and no `apikey`/`Authorization` headers at all.
4. Return `Either<Failure, Uint8List>` — `Right(bytes)` on a 2xx from step 3; any failure from either leg maps
   through `_mapException` (step 1: identical to `call()`'s existing JSON-error path, so `AUTH_EXPIRED`/
   `NOT_FOUND`/etc. all resolve through the normal `ErrorMapper`) or a new, generic retryable
   `NetworkTimeoutFailure` (step 2/3: the storage leg never speaks this app's `{code, message, retryable}`
   error envelope, so there is nothing for `ErrorMapper` to parse — Edge Cases only asks that "the
   corresponding button returns to a retryable state", not that the exact backend error code survive a
   fetch that never reached the backend).

**Rationale**: the signed URL already encodes its own short-lived auth via query parameters (that is the
entire point of a signed URL); forwarding this app's `apikey`/`SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`/user bearer token to a
third-party Storage host it was never intended for is an unnecessary credential-exposure surface Principle
III's spirit ("narrowly-accessed contract... prevents... credential leakage") argues against, and `dio`'s
default redirect-following would do exactly that by keeping the original request's headers across the
redirect. Disabling auto-redirect and manually re-issuing a clean request is the only way to control which
headers reach which host. This mirrors `sseStream()`'s own precedent of adding a second, download-agnostic
transport primitive to `ApiClient` rather than growing a parallel HTTP stack per feature.

**Alternatives considered**: letting `dio` auto-follow the redirect — rejected for the header-leak reason
above; a dedicated plain `http`/`http_client` package call for the storage leg — rejected, `dio` already does
a header-less byte-stream GET with no new dependency; parsing the Storage response as JSON first — rejected,
both `format=pdf` and `format=raw` are binary/text payloads to save to disk, not API responses with a
`{data: ...}` envelope.

## R2 — Saving/sharing the downloaded bytes (no download/file package exists yet)

**Decision**: add `share_plus: ^13.3.1` (new dependency; `path_provider` is already in `pubspec.yaml`, added
for the audio pipeline). A new data-layer class, `ExportFileRepositoryImpl` (behind a domain interface,
`ExportFileRepository`, so `ExportBloc` depends on it through the same mockable-repository shape every other
bloc already uses — never a bare plugin wrapper), writes the downloaded bytes to
`(await getTemporaryDirectory()).path` under a derived filename, then calls `Share.shareXFiles([XFile(path)])`
— the OS share sheet, satisfying the Assumption "trigger[s] the platform's standard way of saving or sharing a
downloaded file." The extension is taken from the response's own `content-type`/`content-disposition` header
when present, falling back to `.pdf` for `format=pdf` and `.json` for `format=raw` (every other endpoint in
this backend's contract speaks JSON; nothing in the OpenAPI spec names a different shape for the raw export).

**Rationale**: Constitution Principle II explicitly leaves "local cache... secure storage" (and, by the same
"choices not fixed here" logic, a file-share mechanism — no fixed package is named for this anywhere in
`docs/input/`) as an open implementation decision, the same category `image_picker`/`record`/`whisper_ggml`
were already added under in earlier units. `share_plus` is the de-facto standard Flutter package for exactly
this job (iOS `UIActivityViewController`), needs no new permission beyond what sharing already implies, and
composes with the already-present `path_provider` rather than introducing a second temp-file mechanism.

**Alternatives considered**: `open_file`/`open_filex` (opens a file in another app directly rather than
offering the OS share sheet) — rejected, narrower than "save or share" and typically requires a file-
association/viewer app to exist, which this PDF-generating unit cannot assume; writing to a permanent
app-documents path and leaving the user to find it in Files.app — rejected, no in-app file browser exists or
is in scope (Assumptions: "not responsible for building a custom in-app file viewer"), so a silent write with
no share/save prompt would be a dead end for the user.

## R3 — Status-polling mechanism and interval

**Decision**: `ExportBloc` polls `GET /export/{jobId}/status` through a self-rescheduling chain of internal
events, not `Timer.periodic` — the exact shape `RecordsBloc`'s own search debounce already establishes
(`Timer(duration, () => add(Event()))`, re-armed from inside the handler, cancelled in `close()`). The instant
`ExportRequested` is handled, the bloc emits `ExportPending()` synchronously (FR-004's "immediately after the
request"), awaits the `POST /export/summary` call, and on success immediately dispatches one
`ExportStatusPollTicked()` (no initial delay — the POST round-trip has already elapsed). Each tick's handler
calls `GET status` once; if the resulting job is not yet in a terminal state (`sheetState` below), it arms
`Timer(const Duration(seconds: 2), () => add(const ExportStatusPollTicked()))` for the next tick. Sequential,
never overlapping — a slow response is fully awaited before the next tick is even scheduled.

**Rationale**: spec.md's own Assumptions state this interval is "an implementation detail, not a product
requirement, as long as it is frequent enough that the user does not perceive the sheet as stuck" — 2 seconds
comfortably satisfies that for an AI-narrative job (seconds-to-tens-of-seconds scale) without hammering the
backend. Routing every tick through the bloc's own event pipeline (rather than a bare `Timer` mutating state
directly) keeps `ExportBloc` testable with `bloc_test` the same way `RecordsBloc`'s debounce already is —
`add()` from a `Timer` callback is this codebase's own established pattern, not a new one.

**Alternatives considered**: `Timer.periodic` — rejected, risks overlapping requests if a status call ever
takes longer than the interval (the sequential self-reschedule shape cannot overlap by construction); a
shorter interval (e.g. 500 ms) — rejected as needless backend load for a job whose fastest realistic path
(empty-period) never reaches polling at all (R6) and whose slowest path is bounded by an AI call, not network
latency.

## R4 — `ExportJob`'s pure sheet-state derivation, and the sixth, Clarification-resolved state

**Decision**: a pure domain extension, `ExportJob.sheetState`, mirrors the already-established
`DateRangeBounds.boundsAt`/`SyncBadge.derive` pattern (a total function over an enum, zero I/O, directly
unit-testable for RNF07) and implements `export-screen-states.md`'s table verbatim:

| `status` | `narrativeStatus` | `sheetState` |
|---|---|---|
| `pending` | (any) | `pendente` |
| `processing` | (any) | `processando` |
| `dataReady` | `processing` | `processando` (Assumption: no early download link; still visually "Processando") |
| `done` | `done` | `concluido` |
| `done` | `failed` or `skipped` | `erroNarrativa` (FR-006 — the prototype's single "Erro" state) |
| `error` | — | `erroCompleto` (FR-007 — the Clarification-resolved sixth state) |

`erroCompleto` is a distinct enum value from `erroNarrativa` even though the prototype's own catalog names
only one "Erro" state — this directly encodes spec.md's resolved Clarification ("reusing the error color/icon
family, with copy distinct from FR-006's... no PDF/raw buttons, and only... Fechar"). `ExportBloc` additionally
reaches `erroCompleto` from two paths `ExportJob.sheetState` never sees at all, because no job/jobId exists
yet at that point: an `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD`-shaped `POST` failure instead maps to a seventh, job-independent
bloc state, `periodoVazio` (R6), and any *other* `POST /export/summary` failure (timeout, offline, rate-
limited, ...) maps directly to the bloc's `erroCompleto` state without ever creating a job (R6).

**Rationale**: putting the five-row mapping in the domain layer as a pure getter (not duplicated inline in
`ExportBloc` or a widget's `switch`) is the same choice `RecordsBloc` already made for `SyncBadge.derive` and
`DateRangeBounds` — directly testable, and the one place this mapping's correctness is asserted. Keeping
`erroCompleto`/`periodoVazio` as *bloc*-level states rather than trying to force them into `ExportJob` is
necessary because both can occur with no `ExportJob` ever existing (a job is never created for an empty
period, and a POST that never got as far as `202 Accepted` never produced a `jobId` to poll).

**Alternatives considered**: reusing one single `erro` state for both FR-006 and FR-007 with a boolean flag —
rejected, directly contradicts the resolved Clarification's explicit "this state MUST be visually and
functionally distinct from FR-006's narrative-only failure" (FR-007); modeling `periodoVazio` as a sentinel
`ExportJob` (e.g. a fake job with no id) — rejected, forces every `ExportJob` consumer to special-case a
value that was never a real job, when the bloc's own sealed `ExportState` already has a natural home for it.

## R5 — Routing every `POST /export/summary` failure other than `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD` to FR-007

**Decision**: if the initial `POST /export/summary` call itself fails with `ExportEmptyPeriodFailure`, the
bloc emits `ExportEmptyPeriod()` (FR-003) and polls nothing. If it fails with `AuthExpiredFailure` after the
repository's one silent-refresh retry already failed, the bloc fires `reauthRequired` (R7) same as every other
failure path in this app, *and* also emits `ExportFailed()` — the session overlay takes over visually (FR-012)
regardless of what state sits underneath it. For every other failure shape (`NetworkTimeoutFailure`,
`NetworkOfflineFailure`, `RateLimitedFailure`, `ValidationFailure`, ...), the bloc emits `ExportFailed()`
(FR-007's generic, job-independent failure state) directly — no job/jobId exists, so "no data was produced" is
true by construction, matching FR-007's own wording precisely.

**Rationale**: spec.md's FRs/Assumptions describe FR-007 only in terms of a job that "fails entirely," which
textually presumes a job exists — but the spec is silent on what happens if the export is never even accepted
in the first place (e.g. the device goes offline the instant the download icon is tapped). Reasonable
technical judgment under Principle I: a request that never produced a job has, definitionally, produced no
data and no narrative — the exact condition FR-007 itself describes — so reusing that same terminal state
(rather than inventing an eighth, undocumented sheet state) is the simplest construction that satisfies FR-010
("Fechar... present... in every one of the five sheet states") without adding a state the prototype's own
five-state catalog, plus the one Clarification-resolved addition, doesn't already cover.

**Alternatives considered**: a distinct "could not even start" state — rejected, no product input describes
one, and FR-007's own generic, errorCode-agnostic copy ("shown the same way regardless of the backend's
specific error code") already reads naturally for this case too; silently retrying the POST — rejected, not
asked for anywhere, and would hide a real failure (e.g. persistent offline) behind an indefinite "Pendente",
directly risking SC-005's "never... indefinitely" guarantee.

## R6 — Why `ExportBloc` is sheet-scoped (one new instance per `showModalBottomSheet` call), not a singleton

**Decision**: `ExportBloc` is `get_it`-registered with `registerFactory` (a fresh instance per
`getIt<ExportBloc>()` call) — the same registration shape `InsertionModalBloc`/`VaultBloc` already use for
their own modal/one-shot screens — and is provided directly above the bottom sheet's content
(`BlocProvider<ExportBloc>(create: (_) => getIt<ExportBloc>()..add(ExportRequested(...)))`, mirroring
`FilterSheet`'s own self-contained-sheet shape). Its polling `Timer` is cancelled in `close()` (same pattern
`RecordsBloc` already uses for its debounce timer); `close()` fires the moment the sheet's `BlocProvider` is
removed from the tree (i.e. the sheet is dismissed), so no poll ever fires for a sheet the user has already
closed — directly satisfying the Edge Case "the app does not keep polling it in background once the sheet is
gone... not treated as the 'current' export if the sheet is reopened." FR-011's "repeated taps... MUST NOT
create multiple concurrent export jobs" is satisfied one layer up, in `_RecordsPageState`: a simple
`bool _isOpeningExportSheet` guard (set before `await showModalBottomSheet(...)`, cleared after) around the
download icon's `onPressed`, identical in spirit to the guard every `IconButton`-triggered async action in
this codebase already needs against a double-tap racing a single `await`.

**Rationale**: the Edge Case's own wording offers two acceptable shapes ("treated as a no-op (or reopens the
same in-flight sheet)"); the no-op-via-guarded-tap shape is simpler and needs no new cross-sheet state
(reusing a leftover job id across sheet instances would directly contradict the Assumptions' own "Reopening the
export sheet afterward is a fresh request; it does not need to return to a leftover job" — the two Edge
Cases/Assumptions together only make sense together if "in flight" here means "the sheet currently on screen,"
not "any job the backend still happens to be processing"). A page-level singleton bloc (reused across sheet
opens, like `EntriesRepositoryImpl`'s `cachedEntries`) was considered and rejected because the ephemeral,
one-shot-per-open shape of the export sheet (Key Entities: "ephemeral... never shown anywhere outside the
export sheet") has no state worth surviving a dismiss — unlike `EntriesRepositoryImpl`'s cache, which exists
specifically to survive across many screen visits.

**Alternatives considered**: a `RecordsBloc`-owned export sub-state (folding export into the existing bloc
entirely) — rejected, conflates two independently-failing, independently-lifetimed concerns into one state
class, the same reasoning RF04's research.md R7 already used to keep `ChatBloc`/`ChatSessionsBloc` apart; a
page-level singleton `ExportBloc` surviving sheet dismissal — rejected per the Assumptions conflict above.

## R7 — Reusing the exact `reauthRequired`/silent-refresh-retry shape, start to finish

**Decision**: `ExportRepositoryImpl` wraps every one of its three calls (`create`/`status`/`download`) in the
identical `_retryAfterSilentRefresh` shape `EntriesRepositoryImpl` already established (exactly one retry via
`SessionRepository.refresh()` on a first-attempt `AuthExpiredFailure`; a second `AuthExpiredFailure` after that
retry is returned as-is, no loop). `ExportBloc` owns its own one-shot `_reauthController`/`reauthRequired`
stream (`StreamController<void>.broadcast()`, closed in `close()`), fired with `if (failure is
AuthExpiredFailure) _reauthController.add(null);` at every call site that can produce one — the exact line
`RecordsBloc` already uses three times over. The sheet widget (`ExportSheet`, a `StatefulWidget`) subscribes
to it in `initState()` exactly as `RecordsPage` already does for `RecordsBloc`, dispatching
`SessionBloc.add(const AuthExpiredDetected())` — `SessionBloc` is provided above `MaterialApp.router` in
`main.dart`, so it is reachable from a bottom sheet's `BuildContext` exactly as it is from any full-screen
route, and the resulting "Sessão expirada" overlay (pushed via the root `NavigatorKey`) renders above the
sheet automatically, needing no export-specific wiring.

**Rationale**: FR-012 asks for exactly this — the existing RF07 mechanism "tak[ing] over exactly as it does
elsewhere on the screen" — so the correct implementation is to reuse the identical mechanism verbatim, not to
build a parallel one. "Resume reflecting the export job's actual status once re-authenticated" falls out of
this construction for free: `ExportRepositoryImpl`'s own retry-after-refresh means a mid-poll `AUTH_EXPIRED`
that the silent refresh *can* recover from is invisible to `ExportBloc` entirely (the very next poll tick
simply succeeds with fresh credentials); only a refresh that itself fails surfaces the overlay, and once the
user re-authenticates through it, the next scheduled poll tick (already armed before the failure, since the
`Timer` from the prior successful tick is independent of this one failing) picks the real status back up with
no bespoke "resume" code needed.

**Alternatives considered**: having `ExportBloc` itself call `SessionRepository.refresh()` — rejected, 
duplicates logic `EntriesRepositoryImpl`/`ChatRepositoryImpl` already centralize at the repository layer,
and would be the first bloc in this codebase to depend on `SessionRepository` directly, contradicting the
established "blocs never touch `SessionRepository`" shape (research.md precedent, `RecordsBloc`'s own
docstring).

## R8 — How the download icon learns the current period, and why no new `go_router` route is added

**Decision**: the export sheet is opened from `RecordsPage`'s existing header `IconButton` (currently an inert
placeholder, `records_page.dart`'s `_Header`), not via a new route. `_RecordsPageState` reads
`context.read<RecordsBloc>().state`'s `dateRange` (a `DateRangeOption`, already RF06's own filter model) at
the moment the icon is tapped, converts it with the already-existing, pure `DateRangeBounds.boundsAt(DateTime.
now())` extension (RF06) into `(from: DateTime?, to: DateTime?)`, and passes those two nullable values straight
through to `ExportSheet(periodStart: ..., periodEnd: ...)` as `showModalBottomSheet`'s builder argument — the
sheet's own `ExportBloc` dispatches `ExportRequested(periodStart, periodEnd)` from its `initState`.

**Rationale**: spec.md's own Assumptions state the export "exports whatever period My Records' own active
date filter currently represents... rather than offering a separate period picker inside the sheet itself" —
`RecordsBloc`'s `dateRange` is already the single source of truth for that filter (FR-002's own wording,
RF06), and `DateRangeBounds` already converts it to concrete bounds for every other consumer that needs them.
Reusing it here needs zero new domain logic. A bottom sheet (not a route) matches both the prototype
("bottom sheet over Tela 4") and this codebase's own precedent for `FilterSheet` — no `go_router` route exists
for RF06's filter sheet either, for the same reason.

**Alternatives considered**: giving `ExportSheet` its own `SessionRepository`-free copy of date-bounds logic
— rejected, duplicates `DateRangeBounds` for no benefit; a new parameterized route (e.g. `/records/export`) —
rejected, same reasoning RF04's research.md R7 already used against a `/home/:sessionId` route: it would force
`go_router` to own state (the active period) a bottom sheet's constructor argument already carries perfectly
well, for a screen that is visually and functionally a modal, not a navigable destination.

25	lcov --extract coverage/lcov.info 'lib/**/domain/**' -o coverage/domain.info

29	dart test/architecture/no_bloc_imports_bloc_test.dart   # ExportBloc must not import RecordsBloc or vice versa
30	dart test/architecture/domain_purity_test.dart          # lib/features/export/domain/** stays Flutter/data-free
31	```
32	
33	`contracts/http-client-download-extension.md`, `contracts/export-repository.md`, `contracts/export-bloc.md`,
34	and `contracts/records-header-export-extension.md` each carry the full scenario table this unit's coverage
35	depends on.

37	## Manual verification (device/Simulator)
38	
39	### Story 1 — Getting a narrative PDF of your entries (P1)
40	
41	1. On "Meus Registros" with at least one entry in the current filter, tap the download icon (header, top
42	   right). **Expect**: the sheet opens immediately showing a spinner and "Preparando exportação...".
43	2. Within a couple of seconds. **Expect**: the sheet transitions on its own, with no tap required, to
44	   "Gerando resumo com IA..." with a progress bar.
45	3. Once the backend finishes both the data and the narrative. **Expect**: a green check, "Resumo pronto", and
46	   two enabled buttons — "Baixar PDF" (filled/primary) and "Baixar dados brutos" (outline).
47	4. Tap "Baixar PDF". **Expect**: the OS share sheet appears offering a PDF file; completing a save/share
48	   produces a readable PDF containing a narrative summary of that period's entries.
49	5. Back in the export sheet, tap "Baixar dados brutos". **Expect**: the OS share sheet appears again, this
50	   time offering the raw-data file, independent of the PDF download that already happened.
51	6. Tap "Fechar". **Expect**: the sheet dismisses; "Meus Registros"' list, filters, and scroll position are
52	   exactly as they were before the download icon was tapped.
53	
54	### Story 2 — Your raw data is never held hostage by the AI narrative (P1)
55	
56	1. For a period with entries, force the narrative generation to fail (timeout/error) while the underlying
57	   data still completes. **Expect**: the sheet shows a red warning, text explaining the AI summary failed but
58	   the data is still available, and **exactly one** enabled button — "Baixar dados brutos" (no "Baixar PDF").
59	2. Tap "Baixar dados brutos". **Expect**: it succeeds, independent of the narrative ever having completed.
60	3. Separately, force the export job to fail entirely (no data produced at all — not just the narrative).
61	   **Expect**: a *visually and textually distinct* failure state from step 1's — reusing the same red
62	   warning color/icon family, but different copy, **no** download button of any kind, and only "Fechar"
63	   available. Confirm the two failure states are clearly distinguishable side by side (take a screenshot of
64	   each if unsure).
65	4. From that full-failure state, tap "Fechar", then tap the download icon again. **Expect**: this opens a
66	   brand-new attempt (Pendente → ...) — not a stuck or repeated failure screen; retrying is "close, then tap
67	   the download icon again," with no dedicated retry control inside the sheet itself.
68	
69	### Story 3 — Exporting a period with nothing in it is handled gracefully (P2)
70	
71	1. Select (via "Meus Registros"' own filter sheet) a period known to have zero entries, then tap the download
72	   icon. **Expect**: the sheet shows "Nenhum registro nesse período." and a suggestion to adjust the filter
73	   **immediately** — never a spinner or a progress bar first, even briefly.
74	2. Confirm no PDF/raw-data download button appears in this state.
75	3. Tap "Fechar". **Expect**: the sheet dismisses with no file ever having been produced, and "Meus
76	   Registros"' own list/filters are unaffected.
77	
78	### Edge cases worth exercising manually at least once
79	
80	- Tap the download icon, then immediately tap "Fechar" while the sheet still shows "Pendente"/"Processando".
81	  Reopen the export sheet right after. **Expect**: a brand-new "Pendente" attempt starts — the dismissed
82	  job's eventual real outcome (if it ever finishes) is simply never shown, and the app is not observed
83	  polling anything in the background once the first sheet is gone.
84	- Double-tap the download icon as fast as possible. **Expect**: exactly one sheet opens, exactly one export
85	  job is created (confirm via backend logs/a debug network inspector if available — no second `POST
86	  /export/summary` fires).
87	- Once "Concluído" or the narrative-only "Erro" is showing, tap a download button, then immediately tap it
88	  again before the first request resolves. **Expect**: only one download/share attempt actually fires; the
89	  button shows a busy/disabled look in between.
90	- With the sheet open and showing "Pendente"/"Processando", force the session to expire (e.g. an expired test
91	  token). **Expect**: the existing "Sessão expirada" overlay appears over the sheet; after re-authenticating,
92	  the sheet resumes polling and eventually reaches a real terminal state — it never stays stuck on
93	  "Pendente"/"Processando" forever.
94	- Once "Concluído" is showing, force the download call to fail after the fact (e.g. simulate the signed URL
95	  having expired). **Expect**: the tapped button returns to a normal, re-tappable state with no crash and no
96	  stuck "loading" look; tapping it again retries successfully once the simulated failure is lifted.

and `contracts/records-header-export-extension.md` each carry the full scenario table this unit's coverage
depends on.

## Manual verification (device/Simulator)

### Story 1 — Getting a narrative PDF of your entries (P1)

1. On "Meus Registros" with at least one entry in the current filter, tap the download icon (header, top
   right). **Expect**: the sheet opens immediately showing a spinner and "Preparando exportação...".
2. Within a couple of seconds. **Expect**: the sheet transitions on its own, with no tap required, to
   "Gerando resumo com IA..." with a progress bar.
3. Once the backend finishes both the data and the narrative. **Expect**: a green check, "Resumo pronto", and
   two enabled buttons — "Baixar PDF" (filled/primary) and "Baixar dados brutos" (outline).
4. Tap "Baixar PDF". **Expect**: the OS share sheet appears offering a PDF file; completing a save/share
   produces a readable PDF containing a narrative summary of that period's entries.
5. Back in the export sheet, tap "Baixar dados brutos". **Expect**: the OS share sheet appears again, this
   time offering the raw-data file, independent of the PDF download that already happened.
6. Tap "Fechar". **Expect**: the sheet dismisses; "Meus Registros"' list, filters, and scroll position are
   exactly as they were before the download icon was tapped.

### Story 2 — Your raw data is never held hostage by the AI narrative (P1)

1. For a period with entries, force the narrative generation to fail (timeout/error) while the underlying
   data still completes. **Expect**: the sheet shows a red warning, text explaining the AI summary failed but
   the data is still available, and **exactly one** enabled button — "Baixar dados brutos" (no "Baixar PDF").
2. Tap "Baixar dados brutos". **Expect**: it succeeds, independent of the narrative ever having completed.
3. Separately, force the export job to fail entirely (no data produced at all — not just the narrative).
   **Expect**: a *visually and textually distinct* failure state from step 1's — reusing the same red
   warning color/icon family, but different copy, **no** download button of any kind, and only "Fechar"
   available. Confirm the two failure states are clearly distinguishable side by side (take a screenshot of
   each if unsure).
4. From that full-failure state, tap "Fechar", then tap the download icon again. **Expect**: this opens a
   brand-new attempt (Pendente → ...) — not a stuck or repeated failure screen; retrying is "close, then tap
   the download icon again," with no dedicated retry control inside the sheet itself.

### Story 3 — Exporting a period with nothing in it is handled gracefully (P2)

1. Select (via "Meus Registros"' own filter sheet) a period known to have zero entries, then tap the download
   icon. **Expect**: the sheet shows "Nenhum registro nesse período." and a suggestion to adjust the filter
   **immediately** — never a spinner or a progress bar first, even briefly.
2. Confirm no PDF/raw-data download button appears in this state.
3. Tap "Fechar". **Expect**: the sheet dismisses with no file ever having been produced, and "Meus
   Registros"' own list/filters are unaffected.

### Edge cases worth exercising manually at least once

- Tap the download icon, then immediately tap "Fechar" while the sheet still shows "Pendente"/"Processando".
  Reopen the export sheet right after. **Expect**: a brand-new "Pendente" attempt starts — the dismissed
  job's eventual real outcome (if it ever finishes) is simply never shown, and the app is not observed
  polling anything in the background once the first sheet is gone.
- Double-tap the download icon as fast as possible. **Expect**: exactly one sheet opens, exactly one export
  job is created (confirm via backend logs/a debug network inspector if available — no second `POST
  /export/summary` fires).
- Once "Concluído" or the narrative-only "Erro" is showing, tap a download button, then immediately tap it
  again before the first request resolves. **Expect**: only one download/share attempt actually fires; the
  button shows a busy/disabled look in between.
- With the sheet open and showing "Pendente"/"Processando", force the session to expire (e.g. an expired test
  token). **Expect**: the existing "Sessão expirada" overlay appears over the sheet; after re-authenticating,
  the sheet resumes polling and eventually reaches a real terminal state — it never stays stuck on
  "Pendente"/"Processando" forever.
- Once "Concluído" is showing, force the download call to fail after the fact (e.g. simulate the signed URL
  having expired). **Expect**: the tapped button returns to a normal, re-tappable state with no crash and no
  stuck "loading" look; tapping it again retries successfully once the simulated failure is lifted.

Depends only on `ExportRepository`/`ExportFileRepository` — never `SessionRepository`, never `RecordsBloc` or
any of its event/state types.

## Event → state sequence

```
ExportRequested(periodStart, periodEnd)
  -> emit ExportPending()
  -> ExportRepository.create(periodStart, periodEnd)
     -> Left(ExportEmptyPeriodFailure)         -> emit ExportEmptyPeriod()                      [terminal]
     -> Left(AuthExpiredFailure)               -> reauthRequired.add(null); emit ExportFailed()  [terminal]
     -> Left(other Failure)                    -> emit ExportFailed()                            [terminal]
     -> Right(jobId)                           -> store _jobId; add(ExportStatusPollTicked())

ExportStatusPollTicked
  -> ExportRepository.status(_jobId!)
     -> Left(AuthExpiredFailure)  -> reauthRequired.add(null); re-arm Timer(2s, add(ExportStatusPollTicked()))
     -> Left(other Failure)       -> re-arm Timer(2s, add(ExportStatusPollTicked())); state unchanged
     -> Right(job) where job.sheetState is:
        pendente     -> emit ExportPending();     re-arm Timer(2s, ...)
        processando   -> emit ExportProcessing();  re-arm Timer(2s, ...)
        concluido     -> emit ExportConcluded(jobId: job.jobId)                                  [terminal]
        erroNarrativa -> emit ExportNarrativeFailed(jobId: job.jobId)                            [terminal]
        erroCompleto  -> emit ExportFailed()                                                     [terminal]

PdfDownloadRequested                             (ExportConcluded only)
  -> no-op if state.isDownloadingPdf
  -> emit state.copyWith(isDownloadingPdf: true, pdfDownloadFailure: null)
  -> ExportRepository.download(jobId, ExportFormat.pdf)
     -> Left(failure) -> (reauthRequired if AuthExpiredFailure) emit state.copyWith(isDownloadingPdf: false, pdfDownloadFailure: failure)
     -> Right(bytes)  -> ExportFileRepository.share(bytes, ExportFormat.pdf)
        -> Left(failure) -> emit state.copyWith(isDownloadingPdf: false, pdfDownloadFailure: failure)
        -> Right(_)      -> emit state.copyWith(isDownloadingPdf: false, pdfDownloadFailure: null)

RawDataDownloadRequested                          (ExportConcluded or ExportNarrativeFailed)
  -> identical shape to PdfDownloadRequested, targeting ExportFormat.raw / isDownloadingRaw / rawDownloadFailure
```

  for that `ExportBloc` instance after reaching one of `ExportConcluded`/`ExportNarrativeFailed`/
